links.outcome: LLM answer differences across patient gender, race, and writing style in synthetic medical queries
links.effect: Only specific (answering, evaluation) LLM pairs yielded statistically significant differences across writing styles, genders, and races; results did not generalize across LLM pairs.
links.quote: We find that LLM annotators exhibit low agreement scores (average Cohen's Kappa $κ=0.118$), and only specific (answering, evaluation) LLM pairs yield statistically significant differences across writing styles, genders, and races.

links.outcome: Inter-annotator agreement among LLM judges in the absence of ground truth
links.effect: LLM annotators showed low agreement (average Cohen's Kappa 0.118), so single-evaluator results may be statistically significant but non-generalizable.
links.quote: We find that LLM annotators exhibit low agreement scores (average Cohen's Kappa $κ=0.118$), and only specific (answering, evaluation) LLM pairs yield statistically significant differences across writing styles, genders, and races.

unlisted_practices: Use multiple LLMs as evaluators (LLM-as-a-judge) and publish inter-LLM agreement metrics to avoid non-generalizable significant results

screen.reason: Evaluates medical LLM hallucination and bias using automated benchmark probing and LLM-as-a-judge pipelines, demonstrating issues with LLM judge evaluation generalizability.
